transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net high-speed broadband technical operations, my name is Edward. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Edward, my name is Hannah Morris. I am paying seventy pounds a month for your top-tier Fibre 900 package, but every single evening between eight and eleven o'clock my download speed throttles down to fifteen megabits per second!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good afternoon Hannah. I can inspect your optical gigabit profile and regional distribution gateway telemetry. Before we examine your speed telemetry, could you confirm your full postal address and your account security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it is 42 Lansdown Crescent, Bath, BA1 5EX, and my security PIN is 6194. My optical ONT unit serial number is SNET-ONT-88419.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Hannah, that confirms your account details. How are your devices connected to the Hub 5 router during these evening slowdowns?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I have an Apple TV 4K connected directly via a Cat 6 Ethernet cable, and three laptops connected via five gigahertz Wi-Fi in the same room because having a reliable home broadband connection is absolutely essential for our daily household work.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So what has occurred is that while your Fibre 900 subscription delivers gigabit throughput during daytime hours, severe congestion or traffic management reduces your speeds to fifteen megabits during peak evening hours between eight and eleven, is that right in accordance with our standard telecommunications network diagnostic procedures.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that is exactly what happens every single night! My family cannot stream 4K movies or play games, and everything buffers continuously so I really appreciate you taking the time to look into these technical details with me today.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Bear with me for a couple of minutes while I query our core optical line terminal and regional BGP aggregation routers in the Bath exchange across all your connected household devices including laptops, mobile phones, and streaming hardware.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for waiting, Hannah. The OLT telemetry indicates your physical GPON optical light budget is pristine at minus nineteen dBm, but our regional aggregation edge router is experiencing high capacity utilization during peak streaming hours to maintain optimal throughput and low latency across the regional distribution network.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am sick and tired of paying seventy pounds a month for gigabit speeds that turn into dial-up speeds every night! I demand an immediate penalty-free contract exit and a full refund of all broadband fees paid for the past six months right now so I really appreciate you taking the time to look into these technical details with me today.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand how deeply disappointing and frustrating it is to experience evening speed degradation when relaxing with family 4K streaming, Hannah. However, because our diagnostic records show your physical connection syncs at full gigabit capacity and the slowdown stems from regional transit node congestion, our service terms require opening an engineering capacity ticket rather than immediate penalty-free termination or full retrospective refunds; what I can do right now is apply an immediate twenty-pound goodwill credit to your bill, re-route your WAN session to our low-latency London peering node, and book a priority node upgrade ticket in accordance with our standard telecommunications network diagnostic procedures.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Well... at least you acknowledged the problem honestly instead of blaming my home Wi-Fi like the last agent did. Twenty pounds credit and re-routing the session is a fair temporary compromise while you fix the node since we depend heavily on this service for remote working and family communications every day.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have applied the twenty-pound goodwill credit adjustment directly to your account ledger right now across all your connected household devices including laptops, mobile phones, and streaming hardware.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Edward. How do we execute the WAN session re-routing?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am sending a remote session termination command to the local broadband remote access server.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The internet light on the Hub 5 router just went amber for a moment.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, that forces your router to re-negotiate a dynamic IP lease on our alternative low-congestion peering ring.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The light is back to solid white. Let me run a speed test on my Ethernet Apple TV...

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What speed result does the Apple TV speed test application report right now, Hannah?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It is showing four hundred and eighty megabits per second! That is thirty times faster than fifteen megabits!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That confirms your traffic is successfully traversing our London secondary aggregation core.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is a massive improvement for tonight.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously regional bandwidth capacity upgrades require physical line card installation in the telephone exchange.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: When will the permanent line card upgrade in the Bath exchange actually be completed?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our core network engineering department has scheduled the Bath optical node backhaul expansion for completion within fourteen business days, installing two fresh 100-gigabit DWDM uplink transceivers.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That extra backhaul capacity will permanently solve the evening peak bottleneck.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have attached your account to automated monitoring ticket NET-44019-B.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What does that automated monitoring ticket do?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It will poll your evening speed tests automatically every thirty minutes and trigger an SMS alert if speeds drop below two hundred megabits.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That will keep S-Net accountable for maintaining throughput.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You can track the Bath exchange engineering progress via your My S-Net mobile app under Network Status.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will keep an eye on the network status page.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Your Hub 5 router features Wi-Fi 6 technology with multi-user MIMO capabilities.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, all our laptops connect with high wireless link speeds.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our gigabit fiber infrastructure supports ultra-low latency ideal for cloud gaming.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The ping times have been under ten milliseconds when speeds are fast.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We also recommend enabling Smart Wi-Fi band steering to optimize device frequency allocation.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will ensure band steering remains active on all our mobile handsets.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The router will intelligently assign five gigahertz channels to eliminate domestic wireless contention.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Edward, fourteen business days is nearly three more weeks of potential evening buffering! I can't believe S-Net sells gigabit packages when your exchange hardware is oversubscribed! It makes me furious to have to wait three weeks for hardware you should have installed months ago!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exchange equipment upgrades are managed according to scheduled engineering maintenance windows.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I hope your engineering team adheres strictly to that fourteen-day deadline.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our engineering field supervision team oversees all overnight exchange maintenance cutovers.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That gives me confidence the work will actually complete on schedule.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before we conclude our call, that account contact telephone number was 01225 440192, correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, 01225 440192 is my home landline.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We have applied the twenty-pound credit, re-routed your WAN session to the London peering ring, verified 480 Mbps throughput, and logged engineering ticket NET-44019-B.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Edward, the speed is vastly better tonight.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there any other aspect of your gigabit broadband service I can assist you with today, Hannah?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our automated network management systems will monitor line jitter continuously.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That continuous monitoring will ensure packet loss remains at zero percent.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our automated network management systems will monitor line jitter continuously.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That continuous monitoring will ensure packet loss remains at zero percent.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No thank you Edward, you have done what you could for now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net high-speed broadband technical operations, Hannah. Have a wonderful evening. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye Edward.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net. Goodbye.
